# Nagaravindeyya Sutta (MN 150 (PTS MN iii 290))

**ID:** MN 150 (PTS MN iii 290)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Nagaravindeyya Sutta
**Title (English, from literature):** With the People of Nagaravinda
**PTS:** MN iii 290
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0203m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Nagaravindeyya Sutta* (MN 150, PTS MN iii 290) is a discourse of the Majjhimanikāya delivered when the Buddha arrived at the Kosalan brahmin village of Nagaravinda while on tour with a large Saṅgha of monks [Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995; McTighe n.d.]. Categorized as a group instruction given to an unspecified gathering of local brahmin householders (*brāhmaṇagahapatikā*) [McTighe n.d.], the sutta addresses which spiritual practitioners are genuinely worthy of veneration, honour, and respect [Humphreys 1956; Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995]. The Buddha clarifies that laypeople should honor only those ascetics and brahmins who are inwardly free, possessing conduct superior to ordinary householders by having eradicated lust, hatred, and delusion, or who are actively practicing for their abandonment [Jackson 1983; Rogell 2003].

 Automatically computed text-reuse data from DharmaNexus identifies 773 matching segments across 73 Pali texts, showing substantial shared phrasing with the *Magga Saṁyutta* (SN 45), the *Tikanipāta* (AN 3), the *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35), as well as near-verbatim opening narrative passages shared with other discourses set in brahmin villages, such as the *Apaṇṇaka Sutta* (MN 60), the *Sāleyyaka Sutta* (MN 41), and the *Brahmāyu Sutta* (MN 91) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns passages of the discourse with two texts in the Chinese *Madhyamāgama* (T 26, discourses 31 and 57) and the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D 3) [DharmaNexus].
